answer: Each identity claims one yarrow plot, locks an 80-credit bond for its river bank, and files each epoch a signed pin reading measured against a horizon sight-line, paying a filing fee. An auditor remeasures sampled pins against the bank-erosion table; a missing, reused, or mismatched reading burns the bond. First filing costs 37 credits, the k-th 37+6(k-1); the 1000th costs 6031, and 1000 fakes cost 3,034,000 plus 80,000 locked. A rented-plot ring fails because one operator cannot attend simultaneous visits at many plots; an honest holder pays 37 once and recovers the bond after an epoch.
